findings: Repeated OOM-kill pattern: 5 OOM-killer mentions, 2 systemd oom-kill failures, restart counter at 4.
Primary leak signature: cache slots created=1,142,003, freed=214, retained=1,141,789, leak fraction=99.98%.
Heap profile points to object_cache_create_slot at 61.2% of allocations; blob_deser_realloc 18.9% and json_decode_workspace 9.4% are secondary contributors.
RSS growth is sustained: samples 2.31G -> 3.87G with growth 212 -> 318 MB/10min; average ~26.5 MB/min.
Cgroup limit breach confirmed: usage 4126MB vs limit 4096MB, over by 30MB, failcnt=2171.
Prior worker reached OOM after ~222.8 minutes; current worker elapsed ~81.6 minutes, projecting ~73-141 minutes remaining before another OOM.
Cache health degraded before OOM: eviction warnings rose to 3880 evictions/60s and hit-ratio fell from 0.11 to 0.05.
Current worker already shows 2 eviction warnings and 0 RSS warnings, so leak recurrence is likely before RSS alerting catches it.
root_cause_hypotheses: Primary: cache eviction/free callback is missing on slot reuse, causing unbounded retention of cache slots and heap growth until the cgroup memory limit is hit.
Secondary: blob_deser_realloc and json_decode_workspace allocation paths contribute additional memory pressure and may also retain buffers.
Contributing: cache_slots=512 configuration is not enforcing a bounded cache under load; eviction slows and hit-ratio collapses as retained slots accumulate.
Operational: repeated OOM restarts are masking the leak rather than resolving it; restart counter 4 indicates recurrence without escalation.
recommendations: Immediately restart svc-ingest or roll back to the last known good build to reset the leaking worker; schedule proactive restart before the projected OOM window if a patch is not ready.
As a stopgap, reduce cache_slots or disable the object cache to slow the leak; only raise the cgroup memory limit temporarily with close monitoring, since it does not fix retention.
Patch the cache eviction path so slot reuse invokes the eviction/free callback; enforce a bounded LRU/TTL cache and verify created-vs-freed slot counts return to a stable ratio.
Audit blob_deser_realloc and json_decode_workspace for retained buffers or missing frees, especially under high eviction and deserialization load.
Add alerts for RSS growth rate, cache slots created vs freed, eviction rate, hit-ratio collapse, and cgroup failcnt; page before the 4GB limit is reached.
Add a memory-leak regression test and heap profiling in CI for cache slot lifecycle and deserialization paths.
After deploy, validate stability by confirming RSS remains flat, hit-ratio recovers, eviction warnings stop, and no OOM-kill occurs beyond the prior ~223-minute failure window.

findings: Two OOM kills confirmed: 01:14:07 (pid 19124, anon-rss 3.98GB, total-vm 9.87GB) and 04:57:26 (memcg usage 4126MB vs limit 4096MB, failcnt 2171, oom-kill constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG).
systemd reports 'Failed with result oom-kill' twice and 'restart counter is at 4' — the service is in a crash/restart loop, not a one-off event.
Cache slot leak quantified: 1,142,003 slots created vs 214 freed → 1,141,789 retained (99.981% retention), ~5,167 slots/min against a configured capacity of 512 (2,230x over capacity).
Heap profile attributes 61.2% of peak RSS (~2.47GB of 4.03GB) to object_cache_create_slot; blob_deser_realloc (18.9%) and json_decode_workspace (9.4%) are secondary amplifiers.
RSS grew 2.31G → 3.87G in 62.8 min (avg 265MB/10min, last sample 318MB/10min); headroom to the 4GB limit was ~133MB, ETA to limit ≈5 min — growth is monotonic and unbounded.

Eviction path is thrashing but ineffective: 3,880 evictions/60s at hit-ratio 0.05 (and 1,421/60s at 0.11) — eviction runs but does not reclaim leaked slots, consistent with a missing eviction callback on slot reuse.
Post-restart workers (06:01, 06:35, 07:23) show the same signature re-emerging (evictions 205→402/60s, hit-ratio 0.09), confirming the leak is deterministic per workload cycle, not a transient spike.
root_cause_hypotheses: Primary: cache eviction callback is not invoked on slot reuse, so slots created by object_cache_create_slot are never freed — unbounded heap growth until the 4GB cgroup limit is hit and the OOM killer sends SIGKILL.
Contributing: cache_slots=512 is only a nominal config value; no hard bound/LRU enforcement exists, so the cache grows ~2,230x beyond its configured capacity.
Contributing: large blob deserialization (blob_deser_realloc 18.9%) and JSON workspace allocations (9.4%) inflate per-slot footprint (~2.3–6.4KB retained per slot), accelerating time-to-OOM.
Aggravating: systemd restart policy restarts the service immediately after OOM kill, re-entering the leak cycle and masking the underlying defect (restart counter 4).
recommendations: 1) Immediate containment: temporarily raise MemoryMax/MemoryHigh for svc-ingest.service (e.g. 6–8GB) OR restart with cache disabled / cache_slots reduced, to break the crash loop while a fix is prepared.
2) Throttle restarts: set StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst and a RestartSec backoff so OOM-killed workers do not hot-loop and amplify load.

3) Code fix (primary): implement the missing eviction callback on slot reuse in the cache path (anchor: cache eviction path missing on slot reuse) and enforce a hard cap of cache_slots=512 with LRU/TTL eviction.
4) Add a memory watchdog: alert on RSS growth rate (>100MB/10min), cache created-minus-freed delta, hit-ratio <0.5, and cgroup failcnt >0 — all four preceded this outage by 1–3 hours.
5) Bound payload sizes: cap blob_deser_realloc and json_decode_workspace inputs (max blob/JSON size, streaming decode) to reduce per-slot footprint and secondary heap pressure.
6) Validate post-fix with a soak test under production-like load: confirm retained slots ≈ 0, RSS plateaus well under the cgroup limit, and no OOM events across at least one full workload cycle.
7) Add heap profiling (tracemalloc/py-spy) to the service image and retain the top-allocation-site summary in crash dumps for faster future triage.

Heap profile corroborates: object_cache_create_slot accounts for 61.2% of allocations, with blob_deser_realloc (18.9%) and json_decode_workspace (9.4%) as secondary contributors.

Eviction warnings show degradation: 23.7 evictions/s with hit-ratio 0.11, escalating to 64.7 evictions/s with hit-ratio 0.05 — cache is thrashing and no longer effective before each crash.

root_cause_hypotheses: Primary: cache eviction callback is missing on slot reuse in the ingest worker — slots are allocated via object_cache_create_slot but never freed, so the cache grows unbounded regardless of the cache_slots=512 configuration.
Secondary: blob_deser_realloc (18.9%) and json_decode_workspace (9.4%) suggest large-blob deserialization churn amplifies per-slot memory footprint, accelerating time-to-OOM.

Contributing: cgroup memory limit (4096MB) is enforced but there is no memory.high throttling or pre-OOM alerting, so the service runs straight into the hard limit and is SIGKILLed rather than degrading gracefully.
recommendations: 1. Immediate: break the crash loop — temporarily raise the svc-ingest cgroup MemoryMax (e.g. 6G) or shed ingest load, and add systemd RestartSec/StartLimitBurst rate limiting to prevent restart thrash while the fix lands.

2. Code fix (highest priority): implement the eviction/free callback on cache slot reuse and enforce the cache_slots=512 bound; add an assertion/metric that created-minus-freed slots never exceeds the configured cap.
3. Add a soak/load test that asserts slot created vs freed parity and bounded RSS over a multi-hour run before redeploying.
4. Instrument memory guardrails: alert at 70%/85% of cgroup limit, export slot created/freed/retained gauges, and set memory.high to throttle before the hard OOM boundary.
5. Review blob_deser_realloc and json_decode_workspace paths — switch to streaming/chunked deserialization or cap blob size to reduce secondary heap pressure.
6. Post-fix verification: monitor eviction rate, hit-ratio, and RSS slope for at least 24h; confirm no recurrence of 'cache eviction slow' warnings and that restart counter stays flat.
